title: In one V1 Deep Dive mouse, population coupling of a neuron predicts its local EM inputs, but pairwise response similarity gives no pair-specific gain after cell-level control
abstract: Question: in mouse V1, do neurons with similar activity connect more often than axon-dendrite proximity predicts, or does a cell-level property explain the link? Approach: we used the Allen V1 Deep Dive data (mouse 409828, EM materialization 1196, 3 two-photon sessions coregistered to EM). We tested 40,162 ordered same-session pairs (193 presynaptic cells with proofread axons, 517 postsynaptic cells, 785 connected pairs). We computed split-half signal correlations, noise correlations and spontaneous correlations for 5 stimulus types. We measured proximity from synapse positions. Pair level: connected pairs had higher noise correlations within presynaptic-cell and proximity strata (natural images z = 4.2, Holm p = 0.0003; gratings z = 3.5, Holm p = 0.005). When we added the mean similarity of the postsynaptic cell to all cells, all odds ratios fell to 1.01-1.06 per SD and all 95% intervals included 1. Natural-movie signal correlation gave no clear effect in any model. Cell level: postsynaptic neurons with higher population coupling received more synapses from coregistered neurons than proximity predicts. The rate ratio was 1.11-1.13 per SD for spontaneous, grating, sparse-noise and grating-noise coupling (permutation p = 0.004-0.005, Holm p = 0.032). Presynaptic coupling did not predict out-degree (rate ratios 0.94-1.01). The result agrees with Okun et al. (2015). Limitations: one animal; the effect is clear in the large superficial session but not significant in the 2 deeper sessions (177 cells); in-degree samples only coregistered inputs; single-session similarity estimates are noisy, so a pair-specific effect below about 0.1 SD is not excluded; the cell-level hypothesis was chosen after the pair-level diagnostic.

display.caption: Population coupling predicts EM in-degree. A, B: observed/expected connections from coregistered presynaptic cells by within-session quintile of coupling (blue: in-degree of postsynaptic cells; orange: out-degree of presynaptic cells; Poisson SE). Expected values come from presynaptic cell x proximity x distance strata. C: Poisson rate ratio per SD of coupling with cell covariates and session terms, 95% CI, for 8 coupling measures.

Pair level. A: connection probability increases with axon-dendrite proximity (output sites of A within 5 um of input sites of B). B: similarity excess of connected pairs (z, exact within-stratum permutation null) for 11 similarity measures and 3 stratifications. C: conditional-logit odds ratio per SD as covariates are added; the effect goes away when the mean similarity of the postsynaptic cell is added.

citations.reason: Okun et al. 2015 reported that population coupling predicts the number of synapses a neuron receives from neighbours (in vitro). Our EM result in a different mouse and with a different method agrees.

Ding et al. 2025 reported like-to-like connectivity beyond axon-dendrite proximity in MICrONS. We test a related pairwise rule in V1DD and find no pair-specific gain after cell-level control; our design has lower power and uses different similarity measures.
